verses.pali: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.185
verses.english: Numbered Discourses 4.185

verses.pali: 19. Brāhmaṇavagga
verses.english: 19. Brahmins

verses.pali: Brāhmaṇasaccasutta
verses.english: Truths of the Brahmins

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate.
verses.english: Once the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha, on the Vulture’s Peak Mountain.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā abhiññātā abhiññātā paribbājakā sippinikātīre paribbājakārāme paṭivasanti, seyyathidaṁ annabhāro varadharo sakuludāyī ca paribbājako aññe ca abhiññātā abhiññātā paribbājakā.
verses.english: Now at that time several very well-known wanderers were residing in the monastery of the wanderers on the bank of the Serpentine river. They included Annabhāra, Varadhara, Sakuludāyī, and other very well-known wanderers.

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṁ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yena sippinikātīre paribbājakārāmo tenupasaṅkami.
verses.english: Then in the late afternoon, the Buddha came out of retreat and went to the wanderer’s monastery on the bank of the Serpentine river.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena tesaṁ aññatitthiyānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ sannisinnānaṁ sannipatitānaṁ ayamantarā kathā udapādi:
verses.english: Now at that time this discussion came up while those wanderers of other religions were sitting together,

verses.pali: “itipi brāhmaṇasaccāni, itipi brāhmaṇasaccānī”ti.
verses.english: “The truths of the brahmins are like this; the truths of the brahmins are like that.”

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā yena te paribbājakā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho bhagavā te paribbājake etadavoca:
verses.english: Then the Buddha went up to those wanderers, sat down on the seat spread out, and said to them,

verses.pali: “Kāya nuttha, paribbājakā, etarahi kathāya sannisinnā, kā ca pana vo antarākathā vippakatā”ti?
verses.english: “Wanderers, what were you sitting talking about just now? What conversation was left unfinished?”

verses.pali: “Idha, bho gotama, amhākaṁ sannisinnānaṁ sannipatitānaṁ ayamantarākathā udapādi:
verses.english: “Well, worthy Gotama, this discussion came up among us while we were sitting together:

verses.pali: ‘itipi brāhmaṇasaccāni, itipi brāhmaṇasaccānī’”ti.
verses.english: ‘The truths of the brahmins are like this; the truths of the brahmins are like that.’”

verses.pali: “Cattārimāni, paribbājakā, brāhmaṇasaccāni mayā sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā paveditāni.
verses.english: “Wanderers, I declare these four truths of the brahmins, having realized them with my own insight.

verses.pali: Katamāni cattāri?
verses.english: What four?

verses.pali: Idha, paribbājakā, brāhmaṇo evamāha:
verses.english: Take a brahmin who says:

verses.pali: ‘sabbe pāṇā avajjhā’ti.
verses.english: ‘No sentient beings should be killed.’

verses.pali: Iti vadaṁ brāhmaṇo saccaṁ āha, no musā.
verses.english: In speaking like this, a brahmin speaks the truth, not lies.

verses.pali: So tena na samaṇoti maññati, na brāhmaṇoti maññati, na seyyohamasmīti maññati, na sadisohamasmīti maññati, na hīnohamasmīti maññati.
verses.english: But they don’t think of themselves as an ‘ascetic’ or ‘brahmin’ because of that. Nor do they think ‘I’m better’ or ‘I’m equal’ or ‘I’m worse’.

verses.pali: Api ca yadeva tattha saccaṁ tadabhiññāya pāṇānaṁyeva anuddayāya anukampāya paṭipanno hoti.
verses.english: Rather, they simply practice out of kindness and sympathy for living creatures, having had insight into the truth of that.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, paribbājakā, brāhmaṇo evamāha:
verses.english: Take another brahmin who says:

verses.pali: ‘sabbe kāmā aniccā dukkhā vipariṇāmadhammā’ti.
verses.english: ‘All sensual pleasures are impermanent, suffering, and perishable.’

verses.pali: Iti vadaṁ brāhmaṇo saccamāha, no musā.
verses.english: Saying this, a brahmin speaks the truth, not lies.

verses.pali: So tena na samaṇoti maññati, na brāhmaṇoti maññati, na seyyohamasmīti maññati, na sadisohamasmīti maññati, na hīnohamasmīti maññati.
verses.english: But they don’t think of themselves as an ‘ascetic’ or ‘brahmin’ because of that. Nor do they think ‘I’m better’ or ‘I’m equal’ or ‘I’m worse’.

verses.pali: Api ca yadeva tattha saccaṁ tadabhiññāya kāmānaṁyeva nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti.
verses.english: Rather, they simply practice for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding sensual pleasures, having had insight into the truth of that.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, paribbājakā, brāhmaṇo evamāha:
verses.english: Take another brahmin who says:

verses.pali: ‘sabbe bhavā aniccā …pe… tadabhiññāya bhavānaṁyeva nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti.
verses.english: ‘All states of existence are impermanent, suffering, and perishable.’ … They simply practice for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding future lives, having had insight into the truth of that.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, paribbājakā, brāhmaṇo evamāha:
verses.english: Take another brahmin who says:

verses.pali: ‘nāhaṁ kvacani kassaci kiñcanatasmiṁ na ca mama kvacani katthaci kiñcanatatthī’ti.
verses.english: ‘I don’t belong to anyone anywhere. And nothing belongs to me anywhere.’

verses.pali: Iti vadaṁ brāhmaṇo saccaṁ āha, no musā.
verses.english: In speaking like this, a brahmin speaks the truth, not lies.

verses.pali: So tena na samaṇoti maññati, na brāhmaṇoti maññati, na seyyohamasmīti maññati, na sadisohamasmīti maññati, na hīnohamasmīti maññati.
verses.english: But they don’t think of themselves as an ‘ascetic’ or ‘brahmin’ because of that. Nor do they think ‘I’m better’ or ‘I’m equal’ or ‘I’m worse’.

verses.pali: Api ca yadeva tattha saccaṁ tadabhiññāya ākiñcaññaṁyeva paṭipadaṁ paṭipanno hoti.
verses.english: Rather, they simply practice the path of nothingness, having had insight into the truth of that.

verses.pali: Imāni kho, paribbājakā, cattāri brāhmaṇasaccāni mayā sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā paveditānī”ti.
verses.english: These are the four truths of the brahmins that I declare, having realized them with my own insight.”

verses.pali: Pañcamaṁ.
